title: Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 10 — Vibhūti-yoga
description: Comprehensive 20-question quiz on the Opulences of the Absolute and Catur-śloki Gītā.

questions.question: In Bhagavad-gītā 10.8, Krishna states 'ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo'. What does this foundational phrase declare?
questions.explanation: In BG 10.8, Krishna explicitly states 'ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate'—He is the original source of all spiritual and material worlds, and everything emanates from Him.
options: Krishna is equal to all demigods in authority
The material world was created spontaneously without a source
Krishna is the source of all material and spiritual worlds
Only the spiritual planets originate from Krishna

questions.question: According to BG 10.2, the great sages and demigods fully understand Krishna's origin through their own independent mental power.
questions.explanation: BG 10.2 states 'na me viduḥ sura-gaṇāḥ prabhavaṁ na maharṣayaḥ'—neither the demigods nor the great sages know Krishna's origin or opulences, because He is the source of all demigods and sages.

questions.question: Who spoke this prayer to Krishna in Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 10 upon hearing the Catur-śloki verses?
questions.quote: You are the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the ultimate abode, the purest, the Absolute Truth. You are the eternal, transcendental, original person...
questions.context: Spoken in Chapter 10 after hearing the four essential verses (Catur-śloki Gītā, BG 10.8-10.11).
questions.explanation: In BG 10.12-10.13, Arjuna speaks these words ('paraṁ brahma paraṁ dhāma pavitraṁ paramaṁ bhavān...') accepting Krishna's supreme position as confirmed by sages like Nārada, Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa.

clues: I am named in BG 10.25 as the prominent representation among all sacrifices (yajñānāṁ).
I involve the quiet, meditative repetition of holy names.
I require no elaborate paraphernalia or fire altars to perform.
questions.explanation: In BG 10.25, Krishna specifies 'yajñānāṁ japa-yajño 'smi'—among sacrifices, He is the chanting of the holy names (Japa-yajña).

questions.question: Which luminous body does Krishna identify as His representation among all luminaries in BG 10.21?
questions.explanation: In BG 10.21, Krishna says 'jyotiṣāṁ raviḥ aṁśumān'—among luminaries, He is the radiant Sun.

questions.question: In BG 10.42, Krishna states that He pervades and supports the entire universe with only a single fragment (ekāṁśena) of Himself.
questions.explanation: In BG 10.42, Krishna concludes 'viṣṭabhyāham idaṁ kṛtsnam ekāṁśena sthito jagat'—He supports the whole universe by a single partial expansion (the Supersoul).

questions.question: Which of the following great authorities are explicitly cited by Arjuna in BG 10.13 as confirming Krishna's supreme, divine status?
questions.explanation: In BG 10.13, Arjuna cites Nārada, Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa as great sages who confirm Krishna's supreme divine position.

questions.question: Arrange the four verses of the Catur-śloki Gītā (BG 10.8 to 10.11) in their exact sequential philosophical progression:
questions.explanation: The Catur-śloki flows sequentially: 10.8 establishes Krishna as the source of all, 10.9 describes pure devotees discussing Krishna with joy, 10.10 explains how Krishna grants them intelligence (buddhi-yoga), and 10.11 describes Krishna destroying their darkness of ignorance with the lamp of knowledge.
items: BG 10.10: 'Teṣāṁ satata-yuktānām...' (Krishna awarding buddhi-yoga to come to Him)
BG 10.8: 'Ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo...' (Krishna as the source of all spiritual and material worlds)
BG 10.11: 'Teṣām evānukampārtham...' (Krishna dispelling ignorance with the lamp of knowledge)
BG 10.9: 'Mac-cittā mad-gata-prāṇā...' (Devotees deriving bliss by conversing about Krishna)

questions.question: Match each broad Vibhūti category (Left) with Krishna's specific representative manifestation in BG Chapter 10 (Right):
questions.explanation: In Chapter 10: Among Vedas Krishna is Sāma Veda (10.22); among Rudras He is Śaṅkara/Śiva (10.23); among priests He is Bṛhaspati (10.24); among trees He is Aśvattha/Banyan (10.26).

questions.question: According to BG 10.10, what cause directly prompts Lord Krishna to grant buddhi-yoga (transcendental intelligence) to a practitioner?
questions.explanation: BG 10.10 states 'teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam / dadāmi buddhi-yogaṁ tam'—to those who are constantly devoted and worship Him with love, Krishna grants the intelligence by which they can attain Him.
options: Extensive academic research into dry secular philosophy
Constant engagement in loving devotional service (bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam)
Rigid execution of ritualistic karma-kāṇḍa sacrifices for personal wealth
Renouncing all human speech and retreating to a mountain cave without devotion

questions.question: Which of the following is the ODD ONE OUT regarding Krishna's representations among Sages/Thinkers in BG Chapter 10?
questions.explanation: Bhṛgu (10.25), Nārada (10.26), and Vyāsa (10.37) are all human/divine sages representing Krishna. Citraratha (10.26) is the chief among Gandharvas (celestial singers), not a sage.

questions.question: Identify the MISSING LINK in Krishna's progression of cosmic manifestations: [10.20: Supersoul] -> [10.21: Sun among luminaries] -> [ ? ] -> [10.23: Śaṅkara among Rudras].
questions.explanation: Following BG 10.20 (Supersoul) and 10.21 (Sun/Marīci), BG 10.22 states that among Vedas He is Sāma Veda, among demigods Indra, among senses the Mind (manas), and in living beings consciousness (cetanā).
options: BG 10.22: Sāma Veda among Vedas & Mind among senses

questions.question: Identify the FALSE statement among the three options below regarding Chapter 10 philosophy:
questions.explanation: Arjuna explicitly states in BG 10.18 that he is NEVER satiated in hearing Krishna's ambrosial words ('tṛptir hi śṛṇvato nāsti me 'mṛtam'). Statement 2 falsely claims he became satiated and asked Krishna to stop.
options: Understanding Krishna as unborn and the supreme master frees a person from all sinful reactions (BG 10.3).
Arjuna felt completely satiated after verse 10.11 and asked Krishna to stop describing His opulences.
Arjuna addresses Krishna as Param Brahma, Param Dhāma, and Pavitram Paramam (BG 10.12).

clues: I am identified in BG 10.30 as Krishna's representative among the Daityas (demons).
Despite being born in a demoniac lineage, I exhibited unalloyed devotion to Lord Viṣṇu from childhood.
My unwavering devotion caused the Supreme Lord to appear as Nṛsiṁhadeva to protect me.
questions.explanation: In BG 10.30, Krishna states 'prahlādaś cāsmi daityānām'—among the Daityas (demoniac family), He is Prahlāda Mahārāja.

questions.question: Which of the following internal, emotional, or intellectual qualities listed in BG 10.4-10.5 originate solely from Lord Krishna?
questions.explanation: BG 10.4-10.5 lists intelligence (buddhi), knowledge (jñāna), forgiveness (kṣamā), truthfulness (satyam), pleasure (sukham), fearlessness (abhayam), non-violence (ahiṁsā), and equanimity (samatā) as all originating from Krishna alone.
options: Māyā-janita Egotism created independently of God

questions.question: A practitioner experiences spiritual dryness and struggles to focus during meditation. Applying the principle of BG 10.9-10.10 (Catur-śloki Gītā), what is the most authentic spiritual action to take?
questions.explanation: BG 10.9-10.10 advises engaging in sravanam and kirtanam in the association of like-minded devotees (bodhayantaḥ parasparam) and serving Krishna with love, whereupon Krishna personally imparts the internal intelligence (buddhi-yoga) to overcome obstacles.
options: Abandon spiritual practices entirely and rely on material wealth to buy peace of mind.
Seek out the association of sincere devotees to discuss and chant Krishna's pastimes (bodhayantaḥ parasparam) with love, attracting Lord Krishna's internal guidance.
Perform dry mental speculation without faith, criticizing scriptural commentators.
Attempt to invent new personal rituals that disregard Vedic paramparā guidelines.

questions.principle: The Supreme Lord is transcendental to material cognition and can only be known by His own revelation: 'svayam evātmanātmānaṁ vettha tvaṁ puruṣottama' (BG 10.15).
questions.question: Based on this principle from BG 10.15, what fundamental truth does Arjuna establish regarding knowing the Supreme Lord?
questions.explanation: BG 10.15 establishes that the Supreme Lord is known exclusively through Himself (svayam eva ātmānaṁ vettha)—He cannot be grasped by material empirical senses or mental speculation unless He mercifully reveals Himself.
options: Anyone with high academic scholarship can fully comprehend God without divine grace.
Demigods and demons understand God's personal form better than God Himself.
The Supreme Lord can only be known by Himself and revealed by His internal potency, not by empirical human speculation.
God is an abstract construction created by human imagination.

questions.question: Match each subtle or abstract manifestation in BG Chapter 10 (Left) with its corresponding category (Right):
questions.explanation: In BG Ch 10: Among purifiers He is the Wind (10.31); among sciences He is Spiritual Science/Adhyātma-vidyā (10.32); among subduers He is Time/Kāla (10.30); among secrets He is Silence/Maunam (10.38).

questions.question: Identify the FALSE statement among the deep theological assertions below from BG Chapter 10 and classical commentaries:
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is FALSE. In BG 10.41, Krishna states that opulent creations are merely a SPARK of His splendor ('mama tejo-'ṁśa-sambhavam'), not His complete form or maximum limit. Statement 1 and 3 are true.
options: In BG 10.20, Krishna identifies Himself as the Supersoul (Ātmā) residing in the hearts of all living entities as Garbhodakaśāyī and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu.
In BG 10.41, Krishna states that opulent and beautiful creations represent the maximum limit and full boundary of His total divine energy.
In BG 10.34, Krishna reveals Himself as both all-devouring Death (mṛtyuḥ sarva-haraḥ) and the generating principle of future manifestations.

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately summarize the ultimate philosophical conclusions of Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 10 (Vibhūti-yoga)?
questions.explanation: Chapter 10 concludes that Krishna is the supreme source of all worlds (10.8), He illuminates His devotees' hearts internally by removing ignorance (10.11), all earthly/celestial grandeur is but a spark of His splendor (10.41), and He pervades the whole universe with a single fragment of Himself (10.42).
options: Krishna is the original uncaused source of all material and spiritual existences (BG 10.8).
The Lord personally dwells within the hearts of His unalloyed devotees to destroy ignorance with the lamp of knowledge (BG 10.11).
All opulent, beautiful, and glorious manifestations across the universe are merely a spark of Krishna's splendor (BG 10.41).
Lord Krishna supports and pervades the entire cosmic creation through a single fragment (ekāṁśena) of His potency (BG 10.42)
